summary: This work demonstrates a direct implementation of the controlled-rotation (CROT) gate for bosonic quantum error correction in circuit QED, using drive-enhanced cross-Kerr interactions between two cavity modes coupled to a transmon. The scheme operates at a single transmon drive frequency and preserves the code-agnostic error-propagation properties essential for rotation-symmetric bosonic codes like cat and binomial codes.
motivation: Prior CROT implementations either rely on composing primitive gates (losing desirable error properties) or are code-specific and difficult to implement, requiring large frequency tunability or photon-number-dependent Hamiltonian engineering. A hardware-efficient, code-agnostic direct CROT gate is crucial for realizing the full potential of bosonic error correction.
method: By driving a transmon simultaneously coupled to two cavities, the authors induce drive-dependent resonances that amplify the effective cross-Kerr coefficient $K_{ab}$ between cavity modes while suppressing self-Kerr effects. Analytical formulas guide identification of working points near two-cavity resonances $D_\mathrm{res} = \sigma_a \delta_{a,d} + \sigma_b \delta_{b,d} + \epsilon_{0,\bar{m}} \approx 0$; exact numerics then optimize the configuration. A second driven transmon cancels residual self-Kerr on one cavity.
result: At the optimized working point ($\delta_d/\alpha = 0.835$, $|\Omega_d/\delta_d| \approx 1$), an on-off ratio exceeding 60 is achieved for the cross-Kerr coefficient with controlled higher-order distortions. In a memory task with the $N=2$ binomial code and $M=1$ cat code, the actual CROT gates achieve break-even operation ($R > 1$) across all dephasing rates at high loss rates ($\kappa \sim 10^{-1}$ µs$^{-1}$), with $\sim 7\%$–$12\%$ fidelity reduction compared to ideal CROTs depending on noise regime.
